A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CapMAS research. All 18 pages, including Appendices A–G, are available and readable; text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable matching of equations, figures, tables, and references.

before.justification: v3 reports original hallucination-detection experiments, human-preference correlations, CapMAS evaluations, and appendix ablations and supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v4 reports CapMAS comparisons in Tables 4–5, human-preference correlations in Table 3, and threshold, fluency, and Self-Refine experiments in the appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 retain identical CapMAS decomposition, proposition checking, thresholding, caption correction, and factuality/coverage evaluation procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same IIW-400 and DOCCI experiments, DCI validation examples, synthetic hallucination scenarios, and captioning/VQA comparisons. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged, including VCD, OPERA, LURE, Volcano, LRV, and SPARC in Table 5; FAITHSCORE and FACTSCORE in Table 3; and Self-Refine in Appendix F.

E3.justification: The model configurations, metrics, five-prompt caption summarization, five-example DCI validation set, and human-evaluation construction remain identical. Appendix A retains the initial 100-image DOCCI sample and caption-pair exclusion procedure.

E4.justification: The position-dependent hallucination analysis, reference-style bias test, threshold ablation, caption case study, fluency evaluation, and iterative Self-Refine analysis are unchanged, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Repeated-decoding counts and uncertainty reporting remain identical. Figure 2 retains binwise means and standard deviations, with the Consistency analysis using 40 stochastic decoding iterations.

E6.justification: Tables 1–11 and the graphical and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, Table 5 reports CapMAS scores of 66.3 CLAIR, 63.4 factuality, and 33.1 coverage in both versions.

T1.justification: The atomic-proposition definition, Equation (1), threshold-defined True/False sets, and factuality ratio T/(T+F) are identical. No mathematical reasoning or proof content changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about CapMAS, separate factuality/coverage evaluation, improved caption factuality, and limitations of VQA-centric benchmarking.

C2.justification: The explanations of increasing text dependence, factuality–coverage trade-offs, evaluator limitations, and coverage loss with weaker fact-checkers remain unchanged. Appendix F.3 retains the same efficiency discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation and hyperparameter details, data-construction instructions, Appendix G prompt templates, and the stated code/data access information are identical.

R1.justification: Section 2, the prior-work comparison in Section 3.1, and the bibliography retain the same works and research positioning. Reference entries move across pages without citation additions or removals.

P1.justification: v4 expands the Acknowledgements to include grant RS-2025-02263754, Human-Centric Embodied AI Agents with Autonomous Decision-Making, and updates version/header text. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds running titles on pages 2–18, and the longer acknowledgment reflows references across pages 10–13. Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–11 retain their displays and placement.

improvement.justification: v4 adds a funding acknowledgment and running headers, with associated reference reflow. The scientific text, experimental evidence, appendices, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. These limited administrative and presentation edits do not materially alter overall paper quality.
